what_this_is: The Workshop rows for pulling a person's messages and saved items from the services they use into their own records, one row per service, all running one mechanism in tools/pull-from-connected-accounts; plus one row that reads back what was pulled. A service is one JSON description in read-data/sources/; the person's token reaches the one process on a private pipe and is never in the request.

payload.label: Pull the messages from the Discord text channels my bot can read into my own records
payload.job: Pull the messages from the Discord text channels my bot can read into my own records
payload.description: Reads the text and announcement channels of every server the bot is in (only those the bot may view and read the history of), newest messages first, and keeps them in your records beside the ones already there: a message pulled twice is kept once, an edited message replaces the older copy, and a renamed channel takes its new title. The bot cannot read anyone's personal direct messages, and a message's text is empty unless the bot has the Message Content setting. Give account (a name for this account, default "default"), and optionally limit, most_pages, most_threads. The held Discord bot token (name discord-bot-token) reaches the one process on a private pipe; it is never shown, printed or stored in your records. Answers status (pulled; partial when some requests failed; needs_login when Discord did not accept the token; unreachable), how many new messages or items arrived, the cursor, and any failed requests in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

account.description: A name that tells this account from your other accounts on the same service (for example work). Default: default.

limit.description: How many messages or items to ask for in one request.

most_pages.description: How many pages of one conversation or list to read.

most_threads.description: At most this many conversations are read in one pull.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages connector for this service (snapshot fold, cursor, paging), merged into one source description and ported

payload.job: Pull the messages my Telegram bot was sent into my own records

payload.label: Pull the posts I bookmarked on X into my own records
payload.job: Pull the posts I bookmarked on X into my own records
payload.description: Reads your bookmarks (newest first; needs a token with the bookmark.read, tweet.read and users.read scopes) and keeps each in your records. payload.label: Pull the Signal conversations my client printed into my own records
payload.job: Pull the Signal conversations my client printed into my own records
payload.description: Keeps the conversations a Signal client on your computer printed (signal-cli output, handed in as conversations) as conversations in your records, with who the account is (self_id). It asks no one and holds no token: the Signal client holds its own login and the transport that runs it is a different row. A message pulled twice is kept once, an edit replaces the older copy, messages stay exactly as printed in time order, and the cursor is the greatest message time seen, which the transport asks the client from next time. Give self_id and conversations, and optionally account (a name for this account, default "default") and most_threads. Answers status (pulled), how many new messages arrived, the cursor, and anything that failed in errors. Read what was pulled with tool:read-what-i-pulled-from-an-account.

self_id.description: The identity Signal knows this account by. A message from it is the account's own.

conversations.description: What the person's Signal client printed: a list of conversations, each { id, name?, type?, messages: [{ id?, timestamp (epoch milliseconds), from, body?, editedTimestamp?, type? }] }.

account.description: A name that tells this account from your other accounts on the same service (for example work). Default: default.

most_threads.description: At most this many conversations are read in one pull.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages signal-bot-connector (snapshot fold, normalization of the client output), merged into one source description and ported; the live client is not here

payload.label: Read what I pulled from a connected account
payload.job: Read the conversations, messages and saved items I pulled from a connected account such as Discord, Slack, Telegram, Signal, Instagram, Messenger, X bookmarks or Pinterest
payload.description: Give source (discord, slack, telegram, signal, instagram-messages, messenger-messages, x-bookmarks or pinterest-pins) and optionally account (the name it was pulled under, default "default"). Without thread it answers the conversations (id, title, message count), the collections (name, count), who the account is, the cursor and when it was last pulled. With thread (a conversation id from that list) it answers that conversation's messages exactly as the service sent them, the last limit of them (default 100, at most 500). It reads your records and changes nothing; it never reaches the service.

provenance.source: new: reads back the parts the pull tools keep
